title: Queue-based microbatch shedding and KV watermarking for sustained high-QPS backpressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: In real traffic patterns we observe sustained high QPS spikes that cause a pathological interaction between continuous microbatching and the KV cache. When the request queue grows, the microbatching window increases latency and the KV cache accumulates large inactive entries leading to GPU memory pressure and increased OOM incidents. Goal: implement a queue-aware microbatch shedding strategy combined with a KV watermarking eviction hint that reduces tail latency, prevents oversized batches, and keeps GPU memory stable under prolonged high QPS. This ticket captures design, prototype, load-testing, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Under synthetic 5x baseline QPS (90th/99th percentile arrival bursts), p99 latency must not regress by more than 10% versus current baseline and p50 should improve by at least 8% for short requests. 2) GPU memory growth must be bounded: no sustained >75% GPU SMEM utilization for >60s. 3) System triggers batch-shedding and issues a KV-watermark hint within 150ms of detecting queue-watermark crossing. 4) Can be toggled per-instance via runtime flag; metrics emitted for shed_count, watermark_evictions, and avg_batch_size. 5) Rollout controlled via canary and automatic rollback on error rate >0.5%.
notes: Design trade-offs: shedding at queue level reduces tail latency but will drop throughput when overloaded; combine with graceful rejection codes and suggestions to clients (Retry-After header).

KV watermarking: implement soft watermark markers (LOW/MID/HIGH) that annotate cache segments; eviction remains LRU-based but is rated by watermark to prefer high-watermark entries for eviction first.
Backpressure policy: three-tier (ALLOW, THROTTLE, SHED) based on smoothed queue length, predicted GPU memory slope, and recent batch sizes.
We should avoid tight coupling between admission controller and model-specific tokenization costs; use normalized cost units (expected_token_ops) in admission scoring.
